journeyMeta.intro: Orthodontic treatment runs in stages, with check-ups planned around where you live.

faqs.q: How long does orthodontic treatment usually take?
faqs.a: Many cases take 12–24 months, but it depends on how complex the bite is, the method (braces or clear aligners) and how consistently the plan is followed. You get an estimate in writing after your examination.

faqs.q: Why are retainers important after orthodontic treatment?
faqs.a: Teeth naturally tend to move back after treatment. Retainers hold the new positions and reduce the risk of relapse, so wearing them as instructed is part of the treatment.

faqs.q: Can I have orthodontic treatment if I live abroad?
faqs.a: Often yes. Clear aligners need fewer in-person visits than braces, and some check-ups can be done remotely with photos. Braces need regular adjustments in the clinic, so we plan the visit schedule with you before you start.

faqs.q: How do I know whether I need veneers or crowns?
faqs.a: Veneers may suit teeth that need a change in shape or colour and still have enough healthy enamel. Crowns are usually considered when a tooth is significantly weakened or heavily restored. The choice is made after an examination.
You receive a written quote after your examination, before any treatment starts. Anything that depends on what we find during treatment is explained and quoted as a range up front.
